svg.title: How Ergo finds a construction by position in S3
svg.desc: Version 0.5.40 already widened its search only as needed, but it used the editor's per-piece storage path. The proposed path reads a single accepted snapshot, uses packed pages where available, and calculates distances from physical bounds without building editable geometry. For 4,096 test bricks and cold caches, packed lookup used 564 object-store GETs and unpacked lookup used 25,207.
svg.text: How Ergo finds a construction by position in S3
The nearest-match rule stays the same. The server changes what it loads to find the match.
Same search: start at the MCP position (x, y, z)
Expand the 3D search box only as needed: ±16 → ±64 → ±256 → ±1,536 world units.
Stop early only when the best match is strictly closer than anything outside the current box.
Before · v0.5.40
After · packed reads and bounded disk reuse
Open the editing working set
Run each search box through the editor’s spatial index.
Fetch individual S3 records
Read spatial references and piece records; fetch meshes
as needed.
Build brick geometry to measure distance
Read one accepted world revision
Find occupied cells and read each cell only once.
Fetch packed S3 pages in batches
Use the viewer’s pages, which group many pieces together.
For unpacked cells, read individual pieces in parallel.
Measure distance to physical bounds
Cache sorted bounds by packed cell hash, not whole meshes.
Result: return the same nearest assembly ID. MCP loads an editable page only if requested separately.
